items.title: Supreme Court Justice Manoj Misra recuses from hearing case between ISKCON Mumbai and ISKCON Bengaluru
items.summary: Justice Manoj Misra of the Supreme Court recently recused himself from hearing a batch of review petitions filed by International Society of Krishna Consciousness (ISKCON) Mumbai seeking reconsideration of the top court’s May 2025 ruling that recognised ISKCON Bangalore as an independent legal entity and owner of the Hare Krishna Temple in Bengaluru [ ISKCON Mumbai vs. ISKCON Bangalore & Ors. ]. A three-judge bench comprising Justices MM Sundresh , Satish Chandra Sharma , and PK Mishra was earlier hearing the case. The Bench was then reconstituted with Justice Manoj Misra replacing Justice PK Mishra. On October 5, the Court informed that Justice Manoj Misra is recusing from the case citing personal reasons and Justice Sharma is also due to retire in November. Hence, the three-judge bench will have to be reconstituted once again. "The Registry is directed to place the papers of the present matters before Hon’ble the Chief Justice of India for reconstitution of a Bench, as one of us, (Hon’ble Manoj Misra, J.) would like to recuse himself from hearing this matter." the Court noted in its order.
